title: Transitivity on generic geometric specialization arrows over a normal base
statement: Let $N$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] that is normal, meaning that every local ring is a domain integrally closed in its fraction field, and let $\eta$ be its generic point [def-sc-generic-point]. Put $K=\kappa(\eta)$ [def-weil-residue-field], choose an algebraic closure $\overline K$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $\bar\eta:\operatorname{Spec}\overline K\to N$ be the resulting geometric generic point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Let $\bar n$ be any geometric point of $N$. Regard $\bar\eta$ and $\bar n$ as points of $N_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], with $2$-morphisms defined by natural transformations of direct images [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. Then $\operatorname{Hom}_{N_{\mathrm{Et}}}(\bar\eta,\bar n)$ is nonempty, and for any two arrows $u,v:\bar\eta\Rightarrow\bar n$ there is an automorphism $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}_{N_{\mathrm{Et}}}(\bar\eta)$ with $u=v\circ\sigma$. Thus the right action on this Hom-set is precomposition $u\cdot\sigma=u\circ\sigma$, with the target geometric point fixed. Neither uniqueness of $\sigma$ nor a free action is asserted. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Let $n$ be the support of $\bar n$ and choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ containing $n$. It contains $\eta$ because every nonempty open contains the generic point. The ring $B$ is a domain by [def-pc-integral-scheme], and is a normal ring in [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]: its local rings are the corresponding local rings of $N$, all normal by hypothesis. In this affine chart $\eta$ corresponds to $(0)$ and $K=\kappa(\eta)=B_{(0)}=\operatorname{Frac}B$, since localization at $(0)$ inverts precisely the nonzero elements of the domain and has zero maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: Tag 0GJ2, section-specialization, reduction to an affine neighbourhood; affine ring identifications are elementary from the definitions.

proof.text: Put $N_{(\bar n)}=\operatorname{Spec}C$ using [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-ring-triples](2)-(3), the same $B$-algebra $C$, with its structural map $B\to C$, is the filtered colimit of the etale $B$-algebras in the residue-triple diagram at $n$. [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples](1)-(2) says this colimit is local. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-etale-colimit-normal-local-domain] applies to the normal domain $B$ and gives that $C$ is a normal domain and $B\to C$ is injective. In particular both rings are nonzero; this argument does not assume that every stage of the colimit is nonzero.

The presentation in Step 2 makes $B\to C$ ind-etale by [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. The prime $(0)\subset C$ contracts to $(0)\subset B$ by injectivity. Apply [lem-trf-ind-etale-residue-separable] at that prime. Since the residue fields at the zero prime of a domain are their fraction fields [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], it gives a separable algebraic extension $L=\operatorname{Frac}C$ of $K=\operatorname{Frac}B$. Only algebraicity will be needed below; $L/K$ is not assumed normal or finite.

By [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-extension-embeds-algebraically-closed], the specified embedding $K\to\overline K$ extends to $L\to\overline K$. Restrict this embedding to $C$. Taking its spectrum gives a map $a:\operatorname{Spec}\overline K\to\operatorname{Spec}C=N_{(\bar n)}$ whose composite to $U\subset N$ is $\bar\eta$, since its restriction to $B\subset K$ is the specified one [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The bijection [lem-trf-point-arrows-strict-local-lifts] sends $a$ to an arrow $\bar\eta\Rightarrow\bar n$. This proves nonemptiness without choosing an automorphism or assuming a finite extension.

Given $u,v:\bar\eta\Rightarrow\bar n$, [lem-trf-point-arrows-strict-local-lifts] gives corresponding lifts, hence $B$-algebra maps $f_u,f_v:C\to\overline K$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Each is injective: if $0\ne c\in C$, algebraicity of $c\in L$ over $K$ gives a relation $a_0+a_1c+\cdots+a_dc^d=0$ with $a_i\in B$ and $a_0\ne0$, by taking a minimal polynomial over $K$ (whose constant term is nonzero) and clearing denominators. If $f_u(c)=0$, applying $f_u$ gives $a_0=0$ in $\overline K$, contrary to the fixed embedding $B\subset K\subset\overline K$; the same argument applies to $f_v$. Therefore the fraction formula $\iota_u(c/d)=f_u(c)/f_u(d)$, and similarly for $v$, extends them uniquely to $K$-embeddings $\iota_u,\iota_v:L\to\overline K$.

source.place: Agent argument from the algebraic extension of Step 3 and the strict-local lifts of Tag 0GJ2.

proof.text: Let $M=\iota_v(L)\subset\overline K$. The isomorphism $h=\iota_u\iota_v^{-1}:M\to\iota_u(L)\subset\overline K$ fixes $K$. The extension $\overline K/M$ is algebraic because $\overline K/K$ is algebraic [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-extension-embeds-algebraically-closed] to $M\subset\overline K$, with target $\overline K$ and base homomorphism $h$. It gives a field homomorphism $\tau:\overline K\to\overline K$ extending $h$, hence fixing $K$, with $\tau\iota_v=\iota_u$. This homomorphism is surjective: for any $x\in\overline K$, its minimal polynomial over $K$ has a finite nonempty set $R$ of distinct roots in $\overline K$; $\tau$ fixes its coefficients and injectively sends $R$ into $R$, so permutes $R$, and $x\in R$ has a preimage. Thus $\tau$ is a $K$-automorphism. This works for inseparable minimal polynomials too, since $R$ is the set of distinct roots.

source.place: Tag 09GU (fields.tex, lemma-map-into-algebraic-closure); the finite-root-set surjectivity argument is the algebraic-closure argument of Tag 09GV (fields.tex, lemma-algebraic-closures-isomorphic).

proof.text: Let $a_u,a_v:\operatorname{Spec}\overline K\to N_{(\bar n)}$ be the two lifts. On coordinate rings $f_u=\tau f_v$, so $a_u=a_v\circ\operatorname{Spec}\tau$ by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Since $\tau$ fixes $K$, the automorphism $r_\tau$ of the generic topos point in [lem-trf-point-arrows-strict-local-lifts] is defined. Its equivariance formula gives $u=\Theta(a_u)=\Theta(a_v\circ\operatorname{Spec}\tau)=v\circ r_\tau$. Set $\sigma=r_\tau$. Finally associativity gives $(u\circ\sigma_1)\circ\sigma_2=u\circ(\sigma_1\circ\sigma_2)$ and the identity acts trivially, so this is the stated transitive right precomposition action with target fixed. No uniqueness or freeness is used.
